analysis: Examined ClusterControlLeadership.swift (head, lines 1-898) and the supplied patch excerpts for ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift. The security-relevant delta in ClusterControlLeadership.swift is additive wire data on the pairing-keyed link control channel: ClusterControlRequest.stopsBefore (line ~830, init at ~831-837), ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked (~871) and ClusterOnboardingLeaderStatus.init(reply:) (~876-878). Both new fields are optional Ints, so older peers ignore them. The lease, claim-supersession, hand-over and fencing logic (lines 277-389, leadershipConfirmed) is not in the changed ranges and was only read for context. stopsBefore can only make the leader skip a `serve` after a later stop, which is fail-safe against an unwanted restart. A paired member could omit it or send a stale count, but that only restores the previous behavior. Link peers are already trusted for control commands under the pairing key, and nothing here touches the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053), prompts (A-001) or the prefix cache (T-041). No new secret, key or plaintext exposure was found. In ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift the excerpts add the stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped closures, both defaulting to no-op or nil, and pass stopsBefore: nil in the provision call (~2852). The remaining hunks (2901-3535) were not visible as text. Open integration questions: whether serveUnlessStopped really checks the stop counter under the same lock the leader's start takes (the doc comment claims so), whether stopsAsked is persisted in the owner-only setup record with no TOCTOU window, and whether stopsBefore decoding rejects negative or oversized values. These concern availability and correctness of cluster stop/start, not confidentiality. The full diff of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift was not supplied, so that file is only partially covered.
